system.description: System is the system that reads it.

component.description: Component is the part of the system, such as a service or a job.

via.description:
Via is how it reads it, such as an environment variable, a file or
a configuration key.

Consumer.description: Consumer is one reader of a value.

id.description: ID is stable and unique, such as "example-app/prod/SESSION_KEY".

name.description: Name is the display name, often the variable or parameter name.

description.description: Description says what the credential is for.

system.description: System is the system that owns the credential.

environment.description:
Environment is "prod", "staging" and so on; empty when one value
serves every environment.

kind.description: Kind is a well-known kind such as KindRandomSecret, or another slug.

status.description: Status is planned, active or retired.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity is how much harm a leak does.

owner.description: Owner is the person or role who creates and rotates it.

issuer.description: Issuer is the service that issues or accepts the credential.

generation.description: Generation says how and where the value is made.

entitlements.description: Entitlements are what a holder of the value may do.

stores.description: Stores are where the value is kept.

consumers.description: Consumers are who reads the value, and through what.

rotation.description: Rotation says when and how the value changes, and what that breaks.

handling.description:
Handling says which lifecycle steps a person does and which a system
does.

revocation.description: Revocation says how to make the value stop working quickly.

exposure.description: Exposure says what someone holding a leaked value can do.

dependsOn.description:
DependsOn lists the IDs this credential is derived from, such as
the password inside a connection string. A holder of this one also
holds those.

reaches.description:
Reaches lists the IDs a holder of this credential can read, use or
replace, such as the parameters a cloud identity may read. With
DependsOn, it gives what a leak exposes in all.

protections.description:
Protections are what guard the credential besides its secrecy, such
as "MFA: hardware key" or "SSO only".

recovery.description:
Recovery says how to regain access when the value is lost, or that
it cannot be.

links.description: Links point to documentation and consoles.

Credential.description: Credential is one secret in one place for one environment.

resource.description: Resource is what it applies to, such as a repository or a path.

access.description: Access is what it may do there, such as "contents: read".

Entitlement.description: Entitlement is one thing a holder of the value may do.

method.description: Method is how the value comes to exist.

spec.description:
Spec describes the value, such as "32 random bytes, hex" or
"RSA 3072, PEM".

where.description:
Where is the place it is generated, such as "the operator's
machine" or a console page.

command.description: Command generates the value, when one command does.

steps.description: Steps are the manual steps, in order.

Generation.description: Generation says how and where a value is made.

generate.description:
Generate is who makes the value: a person running a command or
using a console, or a system such as a provisioning tool.

distribute.description:
Distribute is who gets the value from its primary store to its
consumers, such as a deploy tool rendering it onto a server.

rotate.description: Rotate is who replaces the value when its policy says so.

automation.description: Automation names the systems that do the automated steps.

Handling.description: Handling says who does each step of a credential's lifecycle.

type.description: Type is a well-known issuer such as IssuerGitHub, or another slug.

account.description: Account is the organization, project or account at the issuer.

console.description: Console is the https URL where it is managed.

Issuer.description: Issuer is the service that issues or accepts a credential.

Link.description: Link is a titled https URL.

$schema.description: Schema is the JSON Schema the file names, if any.

credentials.description: Credentials are the entries, in the order given.

Registry.description: Registry is a list of credentials.

intervalDays.description: IntervalDays is the rotation period, for PolicyScheduled only.

procedure.description: Procedure is how to rotate it.

impact.description: Impact is what breaks, or who notices, when it rotates.

Rotation.description: Rotation says when and how a value changes.

type.description: Type is a well-known store such as StoreAWSSSM, or another slug.

role.description:
Role says whether this is the source of truth, a backup or a copy
written at deploy time.

account.description: Account is the account, organization or vault holding it.

path.description: Path is the parameter, secret, item or file name.

console.description: Console is the https URL where the store is managed.

install.description:
Install says how the value gets here: the command or the steps a
person follows, or the system that writes it.

Store.description: Store is one place a value is kept.

title: Credential registry
description: Every credential of a set of systems, without values: what each is for, how and where it is made, what it may do, where it is stored, who uses it and how it rotates.
